boundary_findings.small_scale: At R10-T4 and 200/500 ms, both modes met every deadline and bounded K12 preserved quality, so no real-time advantage over HiGHS was established.
boundary_findings.quality_preserving_deadline_miss: At R16-T4 and 100 ms, bounded K12 preserved the registered quality limits but met only 1 of 30 deadlines, versus 7 of 30 for exact HiGHS.
boundary_findings.closest_deadline_separation: At R32-T4 and 500 ms, exact HiGHS met 0 of 30 deadlines and bounded K12 met 24 of 30, below the required 29 of 30; service, coverage, and objective-per-task losses also exceeded all registered limits.
boundary_findings.dominant_bottleneck: Fixed-K12 candidate construction consumed 74% to 100% of bounded-mode decision time. The current exhaustive dominance stage often costs more than complete-pool enumeration followed by HiGHS at 10 to 16 resources.
boundary_findings.statistical_direction: Across registered budgets, the bounded mode generally reduced quality endpoints and did not produce a robust deadline-hit advantage after Holm correction.

CA-HMCD-Exact.recommended_use: Default for the tested small and moderate scales when its observed deadline is acceptable.

CA-HMCD-BoundedK12-Candidate.recommended_use: Retain as a reproducible control; do not label it a validated real-time mode.

next_required_algorithmic_work: Replace all-pairs dominance testing with an incremental or indexed nondominance procedure.
Stop candidate construction directly at a certified time budget instead of generating and pruning the full intermediate pool.
Use cheap admissible upper bounds before coalition valuation to avoid evaluating candidates that cannot enter the retained top K.
Re-register and rerun the exact-versus-real-time boundary after implementation; do not tune thresholds against the present outcomes.
claim_boundary: The manuscript may report a negative boundary result and the exact-mode operating region. It may not claim that the present fixed-K12 or adaptive-K implementation is a validated real-time solver.
